items.headline: Meta Agrees to $18 Billion Settlement Over Teen Social Media Addiction Lawsuits
items.summary: Meta has agreed to pay up to $18 billion to settle landmark lawsuits brought by dozens of U.S. states alleging that its platforms harm youth mental health through addictive design features. The story is front-page news today because the agreement requires sweeping changes, including strict daily screen time limits and nighttime app restrictions for teenage users on Instagram and Facebook.

items.headline: UEFA Prepares Criminal Complaint Against FIFA President Gianni Infantino
items.summary: European soccer's governing body, UEFA, announced it is preparing a criminal complaint in Switzerland against FIFA President Gianni Infantino over alleged criminal mismanagement. The legal action follows Infantino's controversial and now-abandoned proposal to sell a portion of future World Cup commercial profits to private investors.

items.headline: BBC Confirms the Return of Hit Motoring Show Top Gear
items.summary: The BBC announced at the Edinburgh TV Festival that it will bring back its flagship motoring series Top Gear after pausing production for nearly four years. The show was put on hold following a serious filming crash in 2022, though the broadcaster has not yet revealed who will host the new series [1.1.6].
